collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 45 or older)

collection.description: A villager whose busy years are over notices a bird they never saw before: watch it, or remember the busy years fondly.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: For a long stretch of (his/her) life, (name1) was busy all the time: work, family, building, fixing, carrying, cooking, every single day, dawn to dark. Now things are a little quieter. Today, sitting outside with nothing urgent to do, (name1) notices a bird (he/she) has never seen before, then realizes it's probably been living in that tree for years.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) watches the bird all afternoon. It has a nest. It has a mate. It has a whole life (he/she) never noticed. (He/she) wonders what else (he/she) missed in the busy years. A lot, probably. (He/she) doesn't regret being busy; those years mattered. But (he/she) decides to look up more now. (He/she) starts that very evening, and sees six more birds.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) thinks about the busy years. They were exhausting. They were also full, of noise and people and things that needed doing. (He/she) misses them a little, the way you miss a loud friend who's moved away. It's quieter now. It's different. (He/she) watches the bird and thinks both kinds of years are good, in their way.
